faq.q: Why can't I see Orion in summer?
faq.a: In summer, Orion lies in the same direction as the Sun, so it is up in the daytime sky, hidden by sunlight. Six months later, Earth is on the other side of the Sun and our night side faces Orion.
asks: Where do the stars go in summer?

faq.q: Why do stars rise 4 minutes earlier each night?
faq.a: Earth turns once relative to the stars in 23 hours 56 minutes, about 4 minutes less than a solar day. So each night the same stars rise about 4 minutes earlier, adding up to two hours a month.
asks: Why does the night sky change over the year?

faq.a: A constellation is a group of stars that people imagined as a picture, such as Orion the hunter. Astronomers divide the whole sky into 88 official constellations.

faq.q: Which constellations can you see all year?
faq.a: Those near the celestial pole never set. From Britain and similar northern places, the Plough, Cassiopeia and the Little Bear are visible on every clear night.

faq.q: Do people in Australia see the same constellations?
faq.a: They see many of the same, but upside down compared with northern viewers, plus southern ones like the Southern Cross that never rise in Britain. Their seasons are swapped too.
asks: Can you see the Southern Cross from Britain?

facts: The International Astronomical Union recognises 88 constellations.
Stars rise about 4 minutes earlier each night because Earth's day measured against the stars is 23 hours 56 minutes.
Orion is a winter constellation for northern hemisphere skies.

quiz.say: Why can't we see Orion in the evening sky in June?
quiz.show: Orion isn't seen on June evenings because…

options.show: It is in the same direction as the Sun, so it is up by day
options.say: It is in the same direction as the Sun, so it is up by day

options.show: Clouds always cover it in summer
options.say: Clouds always cover it in summer

quiz.why: In June the Sun lies in front of Orion, so the constellation is above the horizon in daylight, when we can't see it.

wrong.1: Stars in Orion stay where they are; Earth's position changes.
wrong.2: Even on clear June nights Orion isn't visible, because it is up in the daytime.
